zwölf.et: From Middle High German zwölf, zwolf, zwelf, zwelif, from Old High German zwelif, from an original *twelif, from Proto-Germanic *twalif. Compare Hunsrik zwellef, Dutch twaalf, English twelve, Norwegian and Danish tolv.

zwo.et: Zwo was originally feminine of Early New High German zween m, but is now used as a variant of zwei without gender distinction. Compare, however, Luxembourgish zwou, which is still a feminine form of zwéin. The same is true of some German dialects, e.g. in Swit…

zwölfte.et:
From Middle High German zwelfte, from Old High German zwelifto, from Proto-Germanic *twaliftô.
Equivalent to zwölf + -te.

s: a municipality of Lower Austria, Austria
something with a number, value or size of twelve
having twelve sides and twelve angles; dodecagonal

zwölftjüngst.et: From zwölfte + jung, with jung put into the superlative form jüngst.

zwölftältest.et: From zwölfte + alt, with alt put into the superlative form ältest.
